module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Paths
public import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

/-- `G.cycleLengths` is the set of lengths of the cycles in `G`. -/
def cycleLengths {α : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph α) : Set ℕ :=
  {m | ∃ (a : α) (w : G.Walk a a), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = m}

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- `circumference G` is the length of the longest cycle in `G`.
    It is `0` when `G` is acyclic. -/
noncomputable def circumference (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  sSup G.cycleLengths

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: The apparent finiteness restriction at line 29 is not retained: `[Fintype α]` is an unused section variable. `#print` gives `{α : Type u} → (G : SimpleGraph α) → [DecidableRel G.Adj] → ℕ`, so the definition accepts infinite graphs. For `G = (⊤ : SimpleGraph ℕ)`, I proved that `n + 3 ∈ G.cycleLengths` for every natural n, yet `G.circumference = 0`. Thus the function has an additional, undocumented zero case—unbounded cycle lengths—and is not even an upper bound for cycle lengths on its actual domain. This is not the documented acyclic fallback. All existing circumference use sites explicitly restrict to finite graphs, so they avoid this defect.
findings.source_evidence: MathWorld, https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GraphCircumference.html, defines circumference as “the length of any longest cycle in a graph.” Ma–Ning–Zhao, arXiv:2606.03696, Conjecture 1, concerns a graph on n vertices; its preliminaries likewise define circumference using a longest cycle. The reviewed file attempts to introduce `[Fintype α]` before this definition. Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean, `Nat.sSup_of_not_bddAbove`, confirms that an unbounded natural-number supremum is 0. The missing parameter and the infinite complete-graph counterexample were checked in Lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the finiteness assumption directly in the declaration's binders, for example: `noncomputable def circumference {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ := sSup G.cycleLengths`. This retains the intended domain and preserves every current use. If unrestricted infinite graphs are intended instead, introduce an extended circumference whose supremum is taken in `ℕ∞`.

findings.description: In the inspected use-site `FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2605.02731/DeanCycles.lean`, this declaration's docstring credits the k ≥ 6 result to “Liu, Ma and Zhao (2026)”. The first author is Luo, not Liu. The theorem statement and solved status are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13552 lists Yufan Luo, Jie Ma, and Ziyuan Zhao as the authors of “Dean's conjecture and cycles modulo k”; its abstract states that they resolve the conjecture for all k ≥ 6. The bibliography of the cited arXiv:2605.02731 also records “Y. Luo, J. Ma, and Z. Zhao.”
findings.suggested_fix: Change “Liu, Ma and Zhao” to “Luo, Ma and Zhao”, preferably adding the arXiv:2601.13552 reference.

findings.description: The inspected use-site `FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2605.02731/DeanCycles.lean` gives pages 133–139 for its [DeLeSa93] reference, “Cycles of length 0 modulo 4 in graphs”. The correct pages are 37–49. This is only a bibliographic error.
findings.source_evidence: The bibliography of arXiv:2605.02731 gives Discrete Mathematics 121(1–3):37–49 (1993). Crossref's record for DOI 10.1016/0012-365x(93)90535-2 independently gives the same title, authors, volume, and pages.

reformulations.difference: Cycles are represented by based closed walks satisfying Mathlib's `IsCycle`, rather than by unbased cycle subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved `m ∈ G.cycleLengths ↔ 3 ≤ m ∧ cycleGraph m ⊑ G`, using Mathlib's cycle-subgraph characterization. `IsCycle` excludes nil walks and two-edge backtracking, and repeated choices of basepoint or orientation cannot affect a set of lengths. Thus this definition captures exactly ordinary simple-cycle lengths, not circuit lengths or induced-cycle lengths.

reformulations.difference: The statement and its variants express 'longest cycle' by `C.IsCycle` and `C.length = G.circumference`, and express at most k−1 path vertices by `P.support.length + 1 ≤ k`. The paper also assigns circumference 2 to forests, whereas the library assigns 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the use sites' finiteness assumptions, every cycle length is at most the vertex count. I proved that, for a cycle C, equality with circumference is equivalent to every cycle having length at most C.length. For a path, support is duplicate-free, so its length equals the number of distinct visited vertices; for k ≥ 1, adding 1 to this count and bounding by k is equivalent to bounding it by k−1. Finally, `C.IsCycle` implies that G is not a forest, making the differing forest defaults irrelevant. All these local equivalences were proved in the scratch file and apply to the four variants too.

reformulations.difference: The source bounds gaps between consecutive distinct cycle lengths; Lean bounds the gap between every ordered pair of distinct cycle lengths.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All-pairs separation immediately implies consecutive separation. Conversely, for x < y in a subset of ℕ, take its least element z greater than x. Then x and z are consecutive and z ≤ y, so x+k ≤ z implies x+k ≤ y. I proved this equivalence for arbitrary subsets of ℕ, together with the equivalent subtraction form of the gap bound.

reformulations.difference: As in part i, Lean uses all-pairs separation rather than consecutive-length separation, now with an additional large-girth requirement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same proved set-theoretic separation equivalence applies independently to each graph. It leaves the girth requirement and the quantifiers over the requested gap and girth bounds unchanged.

review.notes: Both declarations in the reviewed module were checked. No semantic defect was found in cycleLengths, and no current problem use misinterprets either definition. The source statuses agree with the inspected problem files. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` and the shorter `/workspace/review/counterexample.lean` compile successfully. Checks include empty, one-vertex and two-vertex graphs; acyclic graphs; cycle graphs; a chorded 4-cycle; and the infinite complete graph. The finite maximum characterization and counterexample proofs use no sorry axioms. All experimental files are under /workspace/review; the reviewed module was not modified.

submission.summary: Made `[Fintype α]` an explicit parameter of `circumference` and clarified that its docstring concerns finite graphs. Left `cycleLengths` unchanged. The required compile passes without errors or warnings; scratch checks confirm that infinite vertex types are rejected and the finite-domain behavior is preserved.
